```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
import xgboost as xgb
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_line, geom_abline, labs, theme_minimal,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display
from sportsdataverse.nfl import load_nfl_schedule
from sportsdataverse.nfl.ep_wp import _load_model

def _fetch(url, timeout=600):
    """Fetch bytes, refusing to return a non-200 body.

    Without raise_for_status a 404/500 HTML error page is written under a
    .parquet/.ubj filename, and every later run treats it as valid because only
    file EXISTENCE is checked -- a poisoned cache and a silently wrong document.
    """
    r = requests.get(url, timeout=timeout)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.content

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "docs" / "models").is_dir() or not (ROOT / "models").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
CACHE = ROOT / "docs" / "models" / ".cache"
CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pbp_path = CACHE / "model_pbp_2025.parquet"
if not pbp_path.exists():
    pbp_path.write_bytes(_fetch(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_2025.parquet",
        timeout=600))
pbp = pl.read_parquet(pbp_path)
bst = _load_model("fg_model.ubj")
ros_path = CACHE / "roster_2025.parquet"
if not ros_path.exists():
    ros_path.write_bytes(_fetch(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_rosters/roster_2025.parquet",
        timeout=300))
ros = pl.read_parquet(ros_path).select("gsis_id", "headshot_url").unique(subset="gsis_id")

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))


```

The field-goal model estimates the probability a placekick is **made**, given
the kick distance and roof/era context. It powers the field-goal branch of the
[nfl4th 4th-down decision](fourth_down.md): the EV of attempting a field goal is
this make probability times three points. It is a Python **XGBoost** retrain of
nfl4th's FG model — which was originally an **mgcv GAM spline** — validated
against the converted GAM grid.

This document is compiled: the make-probability curve is scored from the
bundled booster at render time and overlaid on the latest published season's
**empirical** make rates, and the kicker leaderboard scores every 2025 attempt
through the model to compute field goals over expected.

## Model features

**7 features** (`yardline_100`, `fg_roof`, era0..era4); one row per FG attempt
(`play_type_nfl=='FIELD_GOAL'`, 1999–2025). The era one-hot replaces the old
binary `fg_era` so the make-prob curve is era-aware across all kicking eras.
The binary label is `sp` (field goal made).

| Feature | Type | What it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| `yardline_100` | numeric | Snap field position; kick distance is `yardline_100 + 17`. The dominant signal (**monotone ↓**). |
| `fg_roof` | binary | Outdoors (`roof=='outdoors'`) vs indoor/retractable. |
| `era0..4` | one-hot | Kicking era — the make curve has shifted outward era over era. |

## The model

**Algorithm.** XGBoost, `objective=binary:logistic`, shallow trees with a high
`min_child_weight` (the make curve is smooth), **monotone constraint `−1` on
`yardline_100`** (make probability must fall with distance). Replaces the
original mgcv GAM spline.

**Evaluation.** Because the booster step-approximates a spline, parity is scoped
to the **operating domain** (yardline×roof×era cells with ≥1 real attempt):
**corr 0.9802** there (gate ≥0.98), **freq-weighted corr 0.9880**. Full-grid corr
is lower by construction (0.9690) — the booster cannot reproduce the spline's
extrapolation into never-attempted cells; **max abs FG% diff 0.34**. See
[Parity](parity.md).

## The make curve, against reality

```{python}
#| output: false
fga = pbp.filter(pl.col("field_goal_result").is_in(["made", "missed", "blocked"]))
feats = bst.feature_names
def build_fg_features(df):
    out = df.with_columns(
        (pl.col("roof") == "outdoors").cast(pl.Int64).alias("fg_roof"),
        pl.lit(0).alias("era0"), pl.lit(0).alias("era1"), pl.lit(0).alias("era2"),
        pl.lit(0).alias("era3"), pl.lit(1).alias("era4"),
    )
    return out
fgx = build_fg_features(fga)
have = [f for f in feats if f in fgx.columns]
assert set(have) == set(feats), f"feature mismatch: {set(feats) - set(have)}"
X = fgx.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
p = bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=feats))
fga = fga.with_columns(pl.Series("fg_make_prob", p),
                       (pl.col("field_goal_result") == "made").cast(pl.Float64).alias("made"))
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Model make probability vs empirical make rate by kick distance, 2025 attempts (era4, mixed roofs)."
byd = (
    fga.with_columns((pl.col("yardline_100") + 17).alias("dist"))
    .group_by("dist")
    .agg(pl.col("fg_make_prob").mean().alias("model"), pl.col("made").mean().alias("empirical"),
         pl.len().alias("n"))
    .filter(pl.col("n") >= 5).sort("dist")
)
long = byd.unpivot(index=["dist", "n"], on=["model", "empirical"],
                   variable_name="series", value_name="make_prob")
(
    ggplot(long.to_pandas(), aes("dist", "make_prob", color="series"))
    + geom_line() + geom_point(alpha=0.6)
    + labs(x="kick distance (yards)", y="make probability",
           title=f"FG make curve vs reality — 2025 ({fga.height} attempts)")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
brier = float(fga.select(((pl.col("fg_make_prob") - pl.col("made")) ** 2).mean()).item())
base = float(fga["made"].mean())
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame({
        "metric": ["2025 attempts", "make rate", "Brier (model)", "baseline Brier (constant)"],
        "value": [float(fga.height), base, brier, base * (1 - base)],
    }).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Render-time FG evaluation — 2025 attempts scored by the bundled booster",
                subtitle="scored with era4 + roof features; monotone-in-distance by constraint")
    .fmt_number(columns="value", decimals=4)
)
```

## Results — field goals over expected, 2025

```{python}
kick = (
    fga.filter(pl.col("kicker_player_id").is_not_null())
    .group_by("kicker_player_id")
    .agg(pl.col("kicker_player_name").first().alias("kicker"),
         pl.col("posteam").last().alias("team"),
         pl.len().alias("attempts"), pl.col("made").sum().alias("made"),
         pl.col("fg_make_prob").sum().alias("expected_made"))
    .with_columns((pl.col("made") - pl.col("expected_made")).alias("FGOE"))
    .filter(pl.col("attempts") >= 15)
    .sort("FGOE", descending=True).head(10)
    .join(ros, left_on="kicker_player_id", right_on="gsis_id", how="left")
    .with_columns(("<img src='" + pl.col("headshot_url").fill_null("") + "' height='40'/>").alias("headshot"))
)
gt_show(
    GT(kick.select("headshot", "kicker", "team", "attempts", "made", "expected_made", "FGOE").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Field goals over expected — 2025 (min 15 attempts)",
                subtitle="made minus the model-expected makes on the same attempts; kicker identity is deliberately NOT a model feature, so this residual is the kicker")
    .fmt_markdown(columns="headshot")
    .fmt_number(columns=["expected_made", "FGOE"], decimals=1)
    .cols_label(headshot="", kicker="Kicker", team="Team", attempts="Att",
                made="Made", expected_made="xMade", FGOE="FGOE")
)
```

## Where the 0.97 parity actually comes from

The FG model's parity against the R oracle (attempted-cells corr ~0.97) is the
lowest of the boosters, so this section localizes it rather than leaving it as a
headline number. The oracle is the nfl4th `mgcv` GAM, scored over its own grid
and committed at `models/oracles/fg_model_grid_nfl4th.csv` (provenance in that
directory's README); the booster is scored over the same grid here.

**Scope: 2014–2025.** The nfl4th GAM is fit on 2014+ and its grid carries a
two-level era flag that this repo maps onto `era3`/`era4`, so a 1999–2013
attempt matches no grid cell. Comparing those seasons against this oracle would
be comparing them against a model that never saw them; the booster-vs-reality
section further down is the one that runs on all 27 published seasons.

```{python}
#| output: false
ORACLES = ROOT / "models" / "oracles"
grid = pl.read_csv(ORACLES / "fg_model_grid_nfl4th.csv").with_columns(
    pl.col("fg_model_roof").cast(pl.Utf8).str.zfill(2).str.slice(0, 1).cast(pl.Int32).alias("fg_roof"),
    pl.col("fg_model_roof").cast(pl.Utf8).str.zfill(2).str.slice(1, 1).cast(pl.Int32).alias("fg_era"),
).with_columns(
    pl.lit(0).cast(pl.Int32).alias("era0"), pl.lit(0).cast(pl.Int32).alias("era1"),
    pl.lit(0).cast(pl.Int32).alias("era2"),
    (1 - pl.col("fg_era")).cast(pl.Int32).alias("era3"),
    pl.col("fg_era").cast(pl.Int32).alias("era4"),
)
grid = grid.with_columns(
    pl.Series("ours", bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(grid.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(float),
                                              feature_names=feats)))
)

# The cells real kicks actually occupy. Scoped to 2014-2025 deliberately: the
# nfl4th GAM is fit on 2014+ (`_punt_and_fg_models.R`, `seasons <- 2014:current`)
# and its grid carries only a two-level era, which this repo maps onto era3/era4.
# A 1999-2013 attempt is era3=0, era4=0, matches no grid cell, and would simply
# be dropped by the join below -- so the audit says 2014-2025 and means it.
GAM_ORACLE_SEASONS = range(2014, 2026)
att_frames = []
for season in GAM_ORACLE_SEASONS:
    p = CACHE / f"model_pbp_{season}.parquet"
    if not p.exists():
        p.write_bytes(_fetch(
            f"https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_{season}.parquet",
            timeout=600))
    att_frames.append(
        pl.read_parquet(p)
        .filter(pl.col("field_goal_result").is_in(["made", "missed", "blocked"]))
        .select("season", "yardline_100", "roof")
    )
att = pl.concat(att_frames, how="vertical_relaxed").with_columns(
    (pl.col("roof") == "outdoors").cast(pl.Int32).alias("fg_roof"),
    (pl.col("season") >= 2018).cast(pl.Int32).alias("era4"),
    ((pl.col("season") >= 2014) & (pl.col("season") < 2018)).cast(pl.Int32).alias("era3"),
)
cells = att.group_by(["yardline_100", "fg_roof", "era3", "era4"]).agg(pl.len().alias("attempt_n"))
obs = (
    grid.with_columns(pl.col("yardline_100").cast(pl.Int64))
    .join(cells.with_columns(pl.col("yardline_100").cast(pl.Int64)),
          on=["yardline_100", "fg_roof", "era3", "era4"], how="inner")
    .with_columns((pl.col("yardline_100") + 17).alias("dist"))
)

def corr(df, a="ours", b="prob"):
    return float(np.corrcoef(df[a].to_numpy(), df[b].to_numpy())[0, 1])

buckets = (
    obs.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("dist") < 30).then(pl.lit("under 30"))
        .when(pl.col("dist") < 40).then(pl.lit("30-39"))
        .when(pl.col("dist") < 50).then(pl.lit("40-49"))
        .when(pl.col("dist") < 60).then(pl.lit("50-59"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("60+")).alias("bucket"))
)
order = ["under 30", "30-39", "40-49", "50-59", "60+"]
rows = []
for b in order:
    g = buckets.filter(pl.col("bucket") == b)
    rows.append({"distance": b, "grid_cells": g.height, "attempts": int(g["attempt_n"].sum()),
                 "corr_vs_GAM": corr(g),
                 "mean_abs_diff": float((g["ours"] - g["prob"]).abs().mean()),
                 "max_abs_diff": float((g["ours"] - g["prob"]).abs().max())})
by_distance = pl.DataFrame(rows)
```

```{python}
gt_show(
    GT(by_distance.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="FG parity vs the nfl4th GAM, by kick distance",
                subtitle="attempted cells only; the disagreement is not spread across the range")
    .fmt_number(columns=["corr_vs_GAM", "mean_abs_diff", "max_abs_diff"], decimals=4)
    .cols_label(distance="Distance", grid_cells="Cells", attempts="Attempts",
                corr_vs_GAM="corr vs GAM", mean_abs_diff="mean |diff|", max_abs_diff="max |diff|")
)
```

**The residual is the long-distance tail, and nothing else.** Inside 50 yards —
where 10,819 of the 12,788 attempted-cell attempts live — the two models agree
to a mean absolute make-probability difference of 0.005–0.012. From 50 yards the
agreement degrades (0.047), and past 60 it collapses (0.173 mean, 0.347 max) on
**86 attempts across the 12 audited seasons**. That is the whole story of the headline
number: the cells that carry the disagreement are the cells almost nobody kicks
from, which is also why the frequency-weighted correlation (0.988) is so much
higher than the unweighted one.

The mechanism is the one the model card already names, now measured: the GAM is
a smooth spline that keeps extrapolating a graceful decline past the attempted
domain, while the booster is a monotone step function with a
`min_child_weight` floor, so it flattens where it has no data. Neither is
"right" out there — the GAM's long tail is an extrapolation too, not evidence.

Two candidate explanations that the data rules **out**:

```{python}
era = []
for label, expr in [("era3 (2014-17, grid fg_era=0)", pl.col("era3") == 1),
                    ("era4 (2018+, grid fg_era=1)", pl.col("era4") == 1)]:
    g = obs.filter(expr)
    era.append({"slice": label, "cells": g.height, "attempts": int(g["attempt_n"].sum()),
                "corr_vs_GAM": corr(g), "mean_abs_diff": float((g["ours"] - g["prob"]).abs().mean())})
for label, expr in [("indoor / retractable", pl.col("fg_roof") == 0),
                    ("outdoors", pl.col("fg_roof") == 1)]:
    g = obs.filter(expr)
    era.append({"slice": label, "cells": g.height, "attempts": int(g["attempt_n"].sum()),
                "corr_vs_GAM": corr(g), "mean_abs_diff": float((g["ours"] - g["prob"]).abs().mean())})
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame(era).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="The same parity, sliced by era mapping and by roof",
                subtitle="neither slice separates -- the era-cell mapping is not the cause")
    .fmt_number(columns=["corr_vs_GAM", "mean_abs_diff"], decimals=4)
    .cols_label(slice="Slice", cells="Cells", attempts="Attempts",
                corr_vs_GAM="corr vs GAM", mean_abs_diff="mean |diff|")
)
```

The era-cell mapping (the grid's two-level `fg_era` is projected onto era3/era4)
is a natural suspect and it is not the cause — both era slices land at the same
correlation. Roof is a weak effect in the same direction as sample size.

**Against reality, rather than against the GAM, the booster is well calibrated** —
which is the reading that matters for a model in production:

```{python}
#| output: false
fga_all = []
for season in range(1999, 2026):
    # Fetch on miss: the oracle loop above only caches GAM_ORACLE_SEASONS
    # (2014-2025), but the reality analysis spans 1999-2025. Without this a
    # clean render dies on model_pbp_1999.parquet before producing the
    # historical calibration.
    p = CACHE / f"model_pbp_{season}.parquet"
    if not p.exists():
        p.write_bytes(_fetch(
            "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/"
            f"nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_{season}.parquet",
            timeout=600))
    fga_all.append(
        pl.read_parquet(p)
        .filter(pl.col("field_goal_result").is_in(["made", "missed", "blocked"]))
        .select("game_id", "season", "yardline_100", "roof", "field_goal_result")
    )
hist = pl.concat(fga_all, how="vertical_relaxed").with_columns(
    (pl.col("roof") == "outdoors").cast(pl.Int64).alias("fg_roof"),
    (pl.col("field_goal_result") == "made").cast(pl.Float64).alias("made"),
    (pl.col("season") >= 2018).cast(pl.Int64).alias("era4"),
    ((pl.col("season") >= 2014) & (pl.col("season") < 2018)).cast(pl.Int64).alias("era3"),
    ((pl.col("season") >= 2006) & (pl.col("season") < 2014)).cast(pl.Int64).alias("era2"),
    ((pl.col("season") >= 2002) & (pl.col("season") < 2006)).cast(pl.Int64).alias("era1"),
    (pl.col("season") < 2002).cast(pl.Int64).alias("era0"),
)
hist = hist.with_columns(
    pl.Series("p", bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(hist.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(np.float32),
                                           feature_names=feats)))
)
sched_all = load_nfl_schedule(list(range(1999, 2026))).select(
    "game_id", "surface", pl.col("roof").alias("roof_sched"), "temp", "wind", "stadium_id")
hist = hist.join(sched_all, on="game_id", how="left")
by_surface = (
    # Raw labels carry a trailing-space variant ("grass " alongside "grass") and
    # an empty string; grouping the raw column splits grass across two rows and
    # makes the per-surface read ambiguous.
    hist.with_columns(pl.col("surface").str.strip_chars().str.to_lowercase().alias("surface"))
    .filter(pl.col("surface").is_not_null() & (pl.col("surface") != ""))
    .group_by("surface").agg(pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("made").mean().alias("empirical"),
                             pl.col("p").mean().alias("model"))
    .filter(pl.col("n") >= 200)
    .with_columns((pl.col("model") - pl.col("empirical")).alias("bias"))
    .sort("n", descending=True)
)
```

```{python}
gt_show(
    GT(by_surface.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Model vs realized make rate by playing surface, 1999–2025",
                subtitle="surface is NOT a model feature; a large bias here would be a real gap")
    .fmt_number(columns=["empirical", "model", "bias"], decimals=4)
    .cols_label(surface="Surface", n="Attempts", empirical="Empirical", model="Model", bias="Bias")
)
```

Every surface with a usable sample sits within 0.025 of its realized make rate,
and most within 0.01. Per-season bias behaves the same way (mostly under 0.02).
**So the honest verdict on the 0.97: it is a disagreement between two functional
forms in a region neither has data for, not a defect in the shipped model.** It
should not be "fixed" by chasing the GAM into the extrapolated tail.

## Weather and altitude: measured, not modelled

The card lists weather as an absent feature. Here is what it is worth, as a
residual analysis on outdoor attempts (the schedule carries `temp` and `wind`):

```{python}
out = hist.filter((pl.col("roof_sched") == "outdoors")
                  & pl.col("temp").is_not_null() & pl.col("wind").is_not_null()
                  ).with_columns((pl.col("made") - pl.col("p")).alias("residual"))
wind = (
    out.with_columns(pl.col("wind").cut([5, 10, 15, 20], left_closed=True).alias("bucket"))
    .group_by("bucket").agg(pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("residual").mean().alias("mean_residual"),
                            pl.col("made").mean().alias("empirical"), pl.col("p").mean().alias("model"))
    .sort("bucket").with_columns(pl.col("bucket").cast(pl.Utf8))
)
temp = (
    out.with_columns(pl.col("temp").cut([32, 50, 70], left_closed=True).alias("bucket"))
    .group_by("bucket").agg(pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("residual").mean().alias("mean_residual"),
                            pl.col("made").mean().alias("empirical"), pl.col("p").mean().alias("model"))
    .sort("bucket").with_columns(pl.col("bucket").cast(pl.Utf8))
)
gt_show(
    GT(pl.concat([wind.with_columns(pl.lit("wind (mph)").alias("variable")),
                  temp.with_columns(pl.lit("temp (F)").alias("variable"))])
       .select("variable", "bucket", "n", "empirical", "model", "mean_residual").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title=f"FG residual by wind and temperature — {out.height:,} outdoor attempts",
                subtitle="residual = made - model; a monotone gradient is unmodelled signal")
    .fmt_number(columns=["empirical", "model", "mean_residual"], decimals=4)
    .cols_label(variable="Variable", bucket="Bucket", n="Attempts",
                empirical="Empirical", model="Model", mean_residual="Mean residual")
)
```

Both gradients are monotone and material: kicks in under 5 mph beat the model by
**+2.5 points of make probability** and kicks in 20+ mph fall short by **−3.1**,
a 5.6-point spread the model currently attributes to nothing. Temperature runs
the same way (**−4.2** below freezing to **+1.2** above 70°F), though wind and
cold co-occur, so these are not independent effects — a joint fit would split
less signal between them than the two tables suggest separately.

```{python}
den = hist.filter(pl.col("roof_sched") == "outdoors").with_columns(
    pl.col("stadium_id").is_in(["DEN00", "DEN97"]).alias("mile_high"),
    (pl.col("made") - pl.col("p")).alias("residual"))
gt_show(
    GT(den.group_by("mile_high").agg(
        pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("residual").mean().alias("mean_residual"),
        (pl.col("yardline_100") + 17).mean().alias("mean_distance")).sort("mile_high").to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Altitude, by the crudest possible proxy: is the game in Denver?",
                subtitle="Denver kicks beat the model despite being LONGER on average")
    .fmt_number(columns=["mean_residual", "mean_distance"], decimals=4)
    .cols_label(mile_high="Denver", n="Attempts", mean_residual="Mean residual",
                mean_distance="Mean distance (yd)")
)
```

Denver attempts beat the model by **+3.1 points** while being **1.2 yards
longer** on average — the sign and magnitude thin air predicts. This is a proxy,
not an altitude feature: a real one needs a stadium-elevation table, which does
not exist in the nflverse schedule. **The source to use is the USGS Elevation
Point Query Service** (`https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json?x=<lon>&y=<lat>`;
free, no key, US-only, which covers every NFL venue except the international
games) keyed by stadium coordinates, committed as a ~40-row `stadium_id ->
elevation_m` lookup. That table is the missing input; nothing else blocks the
feature.

None of this is a retrain — it is a measurement of what a retrain would have to
gain. Adding `wind`, `temp` and elevation to a model whose only real feature is
distance is a materially different model, and it inherits a new dependency
(schedule weather is missing or wrong for some older games), so it belongs in a
gated retrain rather than in this document.

## Limitations

Distance is everything plus a coarse roof/era shift — **no kicker identity, wind,
or weather**, and the section above quantifies what the last two cost. The
step-function booster does not extrapolate the smooth GAM tail past the attempted
domain, so very long / never-attempted cells should be read with caution (this is
the freq-weighted vs full-grid corr gap). The render-time scoring above pins era4
for the 2025 attempts it scores, which is exact for 2018+.

## Provenance

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `model_type` | fg |
| `objective` | binary:logistic (monotone yardline ↓) |
| `features` | yardline_100, fg_roof, era0..4 |
| `label` | sp (FG made) |
| `training_seasons` | 1999–2025 (23,919 attempts) |
| `lineage` | nfl4th field-goal model (was mgcv GAM) |
| `parity` | attempted-cells corr 0.971 · freq-weighted 0.986 (informational, era-aware full-history) |
| `distribution` | bundled in sportsdataverse |
| `rebuild this doc` | `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM; `uv sync --group docs`) |

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #29):** *the 0.97 parity audit.* The residual is
  the long-distance tail and nothing else: corr vs the GAM is 0.961 under 30
  yards, 0.950 at 30-39, 0.954 at 40-49, 0.864 at 50-59 and 0.679 at 60+ (86
  attempts in the 12 audited seasons). Era mapping and roof do not separate. Against reality
  the booster is well calibrated (per-surface bias <= 0.025), so the number is a
  functional-form disagreement in a region neither model has data for -- an
  honest residual, not a defect to chase.
- **Resolved (2026-09-01, PR #29):** *weather measured.* Wind and temperature
  carry monotone, unmodelled residual gradients (+2.5 to -3.1 points of make
  probability across wind buckets; -4.2 to +1.2 across temperature), and Denver
  kicks beat the model by 3.1 points while being 1.2 yards longer.
- **Altitude still needs a source**, named in the card: a stadium-elevation
  lookup from the USGS Elevation Point Query Service keyed by venue coordinates.
  Until that ~40-row table is committed, "altitude" is a Denver dummy.
- **Kicker aging** remains unexamined; kicker identity is deliberately the FGOE
  residual, which is the leaderboard's point.
- **Known issue:** wind and cold co-occur, so the two weather tables above
  double-count shared signal -- a joint fit would attribute less to each.
